## CODE FROM CHATGPT - NEEDS TO BE ADAPTED TO MAKE A ROSE PLOT

```{r}


# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# Sample data (replace this with your actual data)
set.seed(123)
data <- data.frame(
  compass_bearing = sample(seq(0, 360, by = 10), 100, replace = TRUE),
  distance = runif(100, 1, 10),
  climate_distribution = sample(c("Tropical", "Temperate", "Arctic"), 100, replace = TRUE)
)

# Create the wind rose plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(compass_bearing), y = distance, fill = climate_distribution)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black") +
  coord_polar(start = -pi/16) +  # Adjust start for orientation
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Tropical" = "coral", "Temperate" = "skyblue", "Arctic" = "lightgreen")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right") +
  labs(fill = "Climate Distribution") +
  ggtitle("Wind Rose Plot with Distance and Climate Distribution")


```



Explanation:
aes(x = factor(compass_bearing), y = distance, fill = climate_distribution): Maps your data to the compass bearing (x-axis), distance (y-axis), and the color of the petals (fill).
geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black"): Creates the bars representing the distance.
coord_polar(start = -pi/16): Converts the plot to a circular format (polar coordinates) with an adjustment to start the plot at a specific angle.
scale_fill_manual(values = ...): Specifies custom colors for the different climate distributions.
theme_minimal(): Applies a clean, minimalistic theme.
labs(fill = "Climate Distribution"): Adds a legend title.
You can adjust the colors, axis labels, or other plot elements to fit your data and preferences.
